rationale.conceptual: The method adapts Tiramisu/DenseNet for pixelwise regression of forces with aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty, requiring understanding of Bayesian deep learning, KL divergence loss for log-normal distributions, and custom prediction formulas. It is not off-the-shelf and involves several mathematical and domain-specific components, but the overall architecture is a modification of existing models, not a completely novel algorithmic derivation.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has three main stages (data preprocessing, model training, evaluation) with multiple sub-steps: downloading a Zenodo dataset, applying Tukey mask, thresholding/morphological extraction, augmentation, log-transform, implementing a dense U-Net with two heads, training loop with specific hyperparameters, and per-frame MAE calculation. This is a moderate multi-stage pipeline with dependencies, but no fragile external tool orchestration or many separate tools.

difficulty.reasoning: This task requires implementing a modified Tiramisu dense U-Net for a non-standard regression with uncertainty estimation, including custom loss (KL divergence for log-normal distributions) and preprocessing with Tukey masking, thresholding, and augmentations. The pipeline involves data download, multi-step preprocessing, model training (200 epochs), and evaluation on test cell frames. While the architecture is an adaptation of known networks, the conceptual novelty and careful implementation of the Bayesian components push conceptual difficulty to 3. The execution is a three-stage pipeline with dependencies and non-trivial data processing, rated 3. Training realistically demands a GPU given 200 epochs on 256x256 patches; dataset is a few GBs from Zenodo.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Training a Tiramisu dense U-Net for 200 epochs on 256x256 patches from 12 cells requires a GPU; the paper used four Titan Xp GPUs, but a single modern consumer GPU suffices. The publicly available dataset is approximately 2–5 GB of image/force maps.
